title: How to average while excluding outliers (TRIMMEAN)
task: A mean that one crazy value can't wreck — response times, judge scores, sensor data.

excel.note: 0.2 = trim 20% of the COUNT total, split between both ends (10% top, 10% bottom).

explanation: TRIMMEAN sorts the data, discards the specified fraction from BOTH ends, and averages what's left: trimming 40% of five values drops one from each end (the 2 and the 100), leaving a clean mean of 4 — while the plain AVERAGE of the same data is a useless 22.8. It's Olympic-judging math. The fraction counts total values trimmed, always split evenly; rounding means small datasets may trim fewer than you expect. For asymmetric or rule-based exclusions, AVERAGEIFS with explicit bounds is the transparent alternative — and MEDIAN remains the maximally outlier-proof option.
